blocks.title: Germs and disease
blocks.md: **Pathogens** are germs that cause disease: **bacteria** (cholera, typhoid, tuberculosis), **viruses** (influenza, measles, polio), **protozoa** (malaria) and **fungi** (ringworm). They spread through **air**, **unsafe water and food**, **contact**, and **vectors** (animals such as mosquitoes). Antibiotics work on bacteria, **not on viruses**.

blocks.caption: How malaria is passed on.
blocks.alt: Four boxes joined by arrows: a mosquito bites a sick person, the parasite grows in the mosquito, the mosquito bites another person, and that person may fall ill.

blocks.title: Malaria
blocks.md: **Malaria** is caused by a parasite (*Plasmodium*) spread by the bite of the **female *Anopheles* mosquito**. Symptoms include fever, shivering and headache. Prevention: sleep under an **insecticide-treated net**, remove standing water, clear bush around homes, use window screens. **Anyone with fever should go to a health centre for a test and proper treatment**; do not self-treat with leftover drugs.

blocks.title: Other diseases and protection
blocks.md: **Cholera and typhoid** spread through contaminated water and food: drink safe water, wash hands with soap, cook food well and use latrines. **Vaccination** (immunisation) teaches the body to defend itself against a disease before it meets it; children should receive the vaccines recommended by the national programme at health centres.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Malaria is not caused by drinking dirty water or by eating oily food: it is carried by mosquitoes.
- Antibiotics do not cure colds or flu, which are caused by viruses.
- Vaccines do not cause the disease they protect against.

blocks.title: Break the chain
blocks.statement: Name two actions that stop a household from catching malaria.
steps: Stop mosquitoes biting: sleep under a treated net.
Stop them breeding: empty containers holding stagnant water.
blocks.answer: Use a treated net and remove standing water.

blocks.title: Which germ?
blocks.statement: A child has watery diarrhoea after drinking unsafe well water. Which type of disease is this likely to be, and what should the family do first?
steps: Water-borne diseases such as cholera are caused by bacteria in unsafe water.
The child must take fluids and be taken to a health centre quickly.
blocks.answer: A water-borne disease; give fluids and get medical help.

blocks.title: Habitats and ecosystems
blocks.md: A **habitat** is the place where an organism lives (a pond, a forest floor). All the members of one kind in a habitat form a **population**; all the populations together form a **community**. A community with its non-living surroundings (soil, water, light, temperature) is an **ecosystem**, for example a rainforest or a savannah.

blocks.caption: A food chain: arrows show the direction of energy flow.
blocks.alt: Four boxes joined by arrows: maize, grasshopper, chicken, human.

blocks.title: Food chains
blocks.md: A **food chain** shows who eats whom; the arrow means 'is eaten by' and shows the flow of energy. **Producers** (green plants) make food using sunlight. **Consumers** eat other organisms: **herbivores** (primary consumers), **carnivores** (secondary or tertiary consumers) and **omnivores**. **Decomposers** (bacteria, fungi) break down dead matter and return nutrients to the soil. Many chains join into a **food web**.

blocks.title: People and the environment
blocks.md: Cutting forests, burning bush, overfishing, hunting and pollution can destroy habitats and reduce the number of species. **Conservation** protects them: protected areas such as Korup (rainforest) and Waza (savannah), replanting trees, fishing rules and cleaning rivers. Energy is lost at each step of a chain, so food chains are short.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- The arrow points to the animal that **eats**, not the one that is eaten.
- A food chain always starts with a **producer**, not an animal.
- Decomposers are not 'waste': they recycle nutrients.

blocks.title: Name the roles
blocks.statement: In the chain grass → goat → human, name the producer, the primary consumer and the top consumer.
steps: Grass makes food by photosynthesis: producer.
The goat eats grass: primary consumer. The human eats the goat: top consumer.
blocks.answer: Producer: grass; primary consumer: goat; top consumer: human.

blocks.title: What if the producers disappear?
blocks.statement: Drought kills most of the grass in a grazing area. Predict the effect on goats and humans in the chain grass → goat → human.
steps: Goats have less food, so their number falls.
Humans then have fewer goats to eat.
blocks.answer: Fewer goats and less food for humans.
